## Setup

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(fixest)
library(broom)
library(gt)
library(car)
library(ggplot2)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "figures/", dpi = 300)

getwd()
```

## Data

```{r}
master_national <- read_csv("data/final/master_national.csv")
#master_national <- read_csv("../../data/final/master_national.csv")

```

```{r}
master_national <- master_national %>%
  mutate(
    log_pop = log(tot_pop),
    log_medhhinc = log(medhhinc),
    pct_nonwhite = 1 - pct_white,
    divorced_per_women = divorced_f / married_f * 1000,
    divorced_per_men = divorced_m / married_m * 1000,
    num_open = as.numeric(num_open)
  )
```

## Variable Definitions

**Exposure variables** (the prison-presence measures being studied):

- `prison_present` — binary indicator, any open prison in the county
- `num_open` — count of open prisons in the county (factor)

**Outcome variables** (what the exposure is hypothesized to affect):

- Mortality/distress: `overdose_rate`, `suicide_rate`, `homicide_rate`
- Household/economic: `divorce_rate`, `life_exp_weighted`, `medhhinc`

**Confounders** (pre-existing county characteristics that could affect both
prison siting and the outcomes above):

- `pct_nonwhite`, `log_medhhinc`, `poverty_rate`, `unemp_rate`, `RUCC_2023`, `pct_bachelors_plus`, `log_pop`, `single_parent_rate`


**Mediators** (variables that sit *between* exposure and outcome — plausible
consequences of prison presence rather than pre-existing causes of it). These
are deliberately **excluded** from the main models, since controlling for a
mediator blocks the causal pathway being estimated; they are examined
separately as robustness/mechanism checks instead:

- `correctional_emplvl_rate` — prisons bring correctional jobs, which may affect household dynamics
- `n_deaths`, `n_suicides` (in-custody) — consequences of having a prison, not pre-existing county traits???

## Analysis: Prison Presence (Binary)

Exploratory comparison of county-year outcomes by whether the county has an
open prison. This is a county-year panel (each county appears up
to 6 times), so a plain two-sample t-test treats repeated observations from
the same county as independent, which they are not — p-values here should be
read as a first look, not a final result. The clustered-SE models further
below are the more defensible version for anything reported formally.

```{r}

names(master_national)
vars_to_test <- c(
  "suicide_rate", "overdose_rate", "homicide_rate",
  "life_exp_weighted", "divorce_rate", "medhhinc",
  "poverty_rate", "unemp_rate", "homeown_rate",
  "pct_bachelors_plus", "single_parent_rate", "marriage_rate", "total_rate"
)

labels <- c(
  "Suicide Rate (community)", "Overdose Rate", "Homicide Rate",
  "Life Expectancy", "Divorce Rate", "Median HH Income",
  "Poverty Rate", "Unemployment Rate", "Homeownership Rate",
  "% Bachelor's+", "Single-Parent Rate", "Marriage Rate", "Religion"
)

results <- map2_dfr(vars_to_test, labels, function(v, label) {
  
  d <- master_national %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), !is.na(prison_present))
  
  test <- t.test(d[[v]] ~ d$prison_present)
  
  tibble(
    Variable = label,
    `No Prison` = unname(test$estimate[1]),
    `Prison Present` = unname(test$estimate[2]),
    Difference = unname(test$estimate[2] - test$estimate[1]),
    `p-value` = test$p.value
  )
})

results
```

```{r}
results %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = 2:4, decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = 5, decimals = 4) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "County Outcomes by Prison Presence",
    subtitle = "Two-sample t-tests, county-year observations, 2019–2024"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = `p-value` < 0.05)
  )
```

### Year-by-year comparison

Splitting the pooled panel by year shows whether the pattern is consistent
across time or driven by a specific year.

```{r}
vars_to_test <- c(
  "suicide_rate", "overdose_rate", "homicide_rate",
  "life_exp_weighted", "divorce_rate", "medhhinc",
  "poverty_rate", "unemp_rate", "homeown_rate",
  "pct_bachelors_plus", "single_parent_rate", "marriage_rate", "total_rate"
)

labels <- c(
  "Suicide Rate (community)", "Overdose Rate", "Homicide Rate",
  "Life Expectancy", "Divorce Rate", "Median HH Income",
  "Poverty Rate", "Unemployment Rate", "Homeownership Rate",
  "% Bachelor's+", "Single-Parent Rate", "Marriage Rate", "Religion"
)

for (yr in sort(unique(master_national$year))) {
  
  data_year <- master_national %>%
    filter(year == yr)
  
  results <- lapply(seq_along(vars_to_test), function(i) {
    
    v <- vars_to_test[i]
    
    d <- data_year %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), !is.na(prison_present))
    
    t_result <- t.test(d[[v]] ~ d$prison_present)
    
    tibble(
      variable = labels[i],
      mean_no_prison = t_result$estimate[1],
      mean_prison = t_result$estimate[2],
      difference = t_result$estimate[2] - t_result$estimate[1],
      p_value = t_result$p.value
    )
    
  }) %>%
    bind_rows()
  
  print(
    results %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_label(
        variable = "Variable",
        mean_no_prison = "No Prison",
        mean_prison = "Prison Present",
        difference = "Difference",
        p_value = "p-value"
      ) %>%
      fmt_number(
        columns = c(mean_no_prison, mean_prison, difference),
        decimals = 3
      ) %>%
      fmt_number(
        columns = p_value,
        decimals = 4
      ) %>%
      tab_header(
        title = paste("National County Outcomes by Prison Presence —", yr),
        subtitle = "Two-sample t-tests, single year"
      ) %>%
      tab_style(
        style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"),
        locations = cells_body(rows = p_value < 0.05)
      )
  )
}
```

## Analysis: Prison Presence, County-Clustered Standard Errors

The plain t-tests above treat each county-year row as independent, which
overstates statistical confidence given the panel structure. These models
correct for that by clustering standard errors at the county level, with and
without year fixed effects.

```{r}
vars_to_test <- c(
  "suicide_rate", "overdose_rate", "homicide_rate",
  "life_exp_weighted", "divorce_rate", "medhhinc",
  "poverty_rate", "unemp_rate", "homeown_rate",
  "pct_bachelors_plus", "single_parent_rate", "marriage_rate", "total_rate"
)

labels <- c(
  "Suicide Rate (community)", "Overdose Rate", "Homicide Rate",
  "Life Expectancy", "Divorce Rate", "Median HH Income",
  "Poverty Rate", "Unemployment Rate", "Homeownership Rate",
  "% Bachelor's+", "Single-Parent Rate", "Marriage Rate", "Religion"
)

clustered_results <- lapply(seq_along(vars_to_test), function(i) {
  
  v <- vars_to_test[i]
  
  d <- master_national %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), !is.na(prison_present))
  
  if (n_distinct(d$prison_present) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      variable = labels[i],
      mean_no_prison = NA_real_,
      estimate = NA_real_,
      std_error = NA_real_,
      p_value = NA_real_,
      n = nrow(d)
    ))
  }
  
  model <- feols(
    as.formula(paste(v, "~ prison_present")),
    data = d,
    cluster = ~GEOID
  )
  
  tidy_model <- tidy(model)
  
  intercept_row <- tidy_model %>%
    filter(term == "(Intercept)")
  
  prison_row <- tidy_model %>%
    filter(term == "prison_present")
  
  if (nrow(intercept_row) == 0 | nrow(prison_row) == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      variable = labels[i],
      mean_no_prison = NA_real_,
      estimate = NA_real_,
      std_error = NA_real_,
      p_value = NA_real_,
      n = nrow(d)
    ))
  }
  
  tibble(
    variable = labels[i],
    mean_no_prison = intercept_row$estimate,
    estimate = prison_row$estimate,
    std_error = prison_row$std.error,
    p_value = prison_row$p.value,
    n = nrow(d)
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

clustered_results %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    variable = "Variable",
    mean_no_prison = "No Prison (baseline)",
    estimate = "Effect of Prison Presence",
    std_error = "SE",
    p_value = "p-value",
    n = "N"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(mean_no_prison, estimate, std_error),
    decimals = 3
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = p_value,
    decimals = 4
  ) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Effect of Prison Presence on County Outcomes",
    subtitle = "OLS with county-clustered standard errors, 2019-2024"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = p_value < 0.05)
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#ffe0b3"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = p_value >= 0.05 & p_value < 0.10)
  )
```

```{r}
clustered_results_fe <- lapply(seq_along(vars_to_test), function(i) {
  
  v <- vars_to_test[i]
  
  d <- master_national %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), !is.na(prison_present))
  
  if (n_distinct(d$prison_present) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      variable = labels[i],
      estimate = NA_real_,
      std_error = NA_real_,
      p_value = NA_real_,
      n = nrow(d)
    ))
  }
  
  model <- feols(
    as.formula(paste(v, "~ prison_present | year")),
    data = d,
    cluster = ~GEOID
  )
  
  tidy_model <- tidy(model)
  
  prison_row <- tidy_model %>%
    filter(term == "prison_present")
  
  if (nrow(prison_row) == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      variable = labels[i],
      estimate = NA_real_,
      std_error = NA_real_,
      p_value = NA_real_,
      n = nrow(d)
    ))
  }
  
  tibble(
    variable = labels[i],
    estimate = prison_row$estimate,
    std_error = prison_row$std.error,
    p_value = prison_row$p.value,
    n = nrow(d)
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

clustered_results_fe %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    variable = "Variable",
    estimate = "Effect of Prison Presence",
    std_error = "SE",
    p_value = "p-value",
    n = "N"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(estimate, std_error),
    decimals = 3
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = p_value,
    decimals = 4
  ) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Effect of Prison Presence on County Outcomes",
    subtitle = "OLS with year fixed effects, county-clustered SEs, 2019-2024"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = p_value < 0.05)
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#ffe0b3"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = p_value >= 0.05 & p_value < 0.10)
  )
```

library(gt)
library(dplyr)

vif_df <- tibble(
  Term        = c("log_medhhinc", "poverty_rate", "unemp_rate",
                   "pct_bachelors_plus", "log_pop", "marriage_rate", "avg_hh_size"),
  VIF         = c(1.28, 1.20, 1.03, 1.05, 1.06, 1.34, 1.30),
  `VIF 95% CI` = c("[1.26, 1.31]", "[1.19, 1.23]", "[1.02, 1.05]",
                    "[1.04, 1.07]", "[1.05, 1.08]", "[1.32, 1.37]", "[1.28, 1.32]"),
  `Adj. VIF`  = c(1.13, 1.10, 1.02, 1.03, 1.03, 1.16, 1.14),
  Tolerance   = c(0.78, 0.83, 0.97, 0.95, 0.94, 0.75, 0.77),
  `Tolerance 95% CI` = c("[0.77, 0.79]", "[0.82, 0.84]", "[0.95, 0.98]",
                          "[0.93, 0.96]", "[0.93, 0.96]", "[0.73, 0.76]", "[0.76, 0.78]")
)

vif_table <- vif_df %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Multicollinearity Check",
    subtitle = "(VIF < 2)"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(VIF, `Adj. VIF`, Tolerance), decimals = 2) %>%
  cols_align(align = "right", columns = c(VIF, `Adj. VIF`, Tolerance)) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.border.top.style = "solid",

    column_labels.border.bottom.style = "solid",
    table.font.size = 14
  )

  ) %>%

    locations = cells_body(rows = p.value < 0.05)
  ) %>%
  tab_style(

  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = p.value < 0.05)
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#ffe0b3"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = p.value >= 0.05 & p.value < 0.10)
  )

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readxl)

# 1. Read and prep the divorce file
divorce_2019 <- read_excel("data/CL-Mar-Div-2011-2019.xlsx", sheet = "Data") %>%
  mutate(
    GEOID = sprintf("%02d%03d", as.integer(STATEFP), as.integer(COUNTYFP)),
    true_divorce_events_2019 = D2019,
    has_2019_data = !is.na(D2019)
  ) %>%
  select(GEOID, true_divorce_events_2019, has_2019_data)

# 2. Filter your main data to 2019 and merge
master_2019 <- master_national %>%
  filter(year == 2019) %>%
  left_join(divorce_2019, by = "GEOID")

# 3. Now check overlap with your prison counties
table(master_2019$has_2019_data, master_2019$num_open > 0, useNA = "always")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Restrict to counties with real 2019 divorce-event data
validation_sample <- master_2019 %>%
  filter(has_2019_data == TRUE, !is.na(tot_pop), tot_pop > 0)

# 2. Build a true crude divorce rate from the event counts
#    (divorces that actually happened in 2019, per 1,000 total population)
validation_sample <- validation_sample %>%
  mutate(true_divorce_rate_2019 = true_divorce_events_2019 / tot_pop * 1000)

divorce_2019 <- divorce_2019 %>%
  mutate(true_divorce_events_2019 = na_if(true_divorce_events_2019, -9))

summary(divorce_2019$true_divorce_events_2019)

# 3. Correlate against your stock-based measure(s)
#    Note: divorce_rate (your "Full" model DV) is per 100, so multiply by 10
#    to put it on the same per-1,000 scale — though correlation itself is
#    scale-invariant, this just makes the scatterplot intuitive
validation_sample <- validation_sample %>%
  mutate(stock_rate_per1000 = divorce_rate * 10)

cor.test(validation_sample$stock_rate_per1000, validation_sample$true_divorce_rate_2019)
cor.test(validation_sample$stock_rate_per1000, validation_sample$true_divorce_rate_2019, method = "spearman")

# 4. Visualize it
ggplot(validation_sample, aes(x = true_divorce_rate_2019, y = stock_rate_per1000)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Stock-based divorce measure vs. true 2019 divorce events",
    x = "True divorce rate (events per 1,000 pop, 2019)",
    y = "Stock-based divorce measure (per 1,000 pop)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# validation_sample already has: has_2019_data == TRUE, tot_pop >= 5000,
# outlier counties excluded, and true_divorce_rate_2019 built

model_2019_true <- lm(
  true_divorce_rate_2019 ~ num_open + pct_nonwhite + log_medhhinc + poverty_rate +
    unemp_rate + RUCC_2023 + pct_bachelors_plus + log_pop +
    marriage_rate + total_rate + avg_hh_size,
  data = validation_sample
)

summary(model_2019_true)

# Cluster-robust SEs aren't really needed here since it's cross-sectional
# (one row per county, no repeated observations to cluster on), but if
# you want heteroskedasticity-robust SEs for comparability with your panel:
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
coeftest(model_2019_true, vcov = vcovHC(model_2019_true, type = "HC1"))

# Tidy summary table, same style as your other results
tidy(model_2019_true, conf.int = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(gt)
library(broom)
library(dplyr)

# Use robust SEs to match your panel models' "county-clustered SEs" rigor
# (here it's HC1 since there's no clustering structure in a single cross-section)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

robust_results <- coeftest(model_2019_true, vcov = vcovHC(model_2019_true, type = "HC1"))

results_df <- tibble(
  Term     = rownames(robust_results),
  Estimate = robust_results[, "Estimate"],
  SE       = robust_results[, "Std. Error"],
  `t value` = robust_results[, "t value"],
  `p-value` = robust_results[, "Pr(>|t|)"]
)

n_obs <- nobs(model_2019_true)

gt_table <- results_df %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "True Divorce Rate (2019) — Validation Model",
    subtitle = paste0("OLS, robust SEs, N = ", n_obs)
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(Estimate, SE, `t value`), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = `p-value`, decimals = 4) %>%
  cols_align(align = "right", columns = c(Estimate, SE, `t value`, `p-value`)) %>%
  data_color(
    columns = everything(),
    rows = seq(1, nrow(results_df), by = 2),
    colors = scales::col_factor(palette = "#FBEEC1", domain = NULL)
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.border.top.style = "solid",
    table.border.bottom.style = "solid",
    column_labels.border.bottom.style = "solid",
    table.font.size = 14
  )

gt_table
```
